title: Modern Java from Java 17/21 to Java 25
topic: Modern Java from Java 17/21 to Java 25
summary: A small, focused tour of what actually changed between the Java 17/21 world most teams stand in and the Java 25 LTS: records, sealed types and pattern matching, virtual threads, scoped values and (preview) structured concurrency, the FFM API, and the JFR/AOT tooling to prove any of it helped — ending in one Java 17 service modernized step by step.

concepts.title: Records and Data-First Design
concepts.unit: Part I — The shapes you declare
concepts.brief: Replace boilerplate DTOs and value objects with records; compact constructors and validation; records vs ordinary classes.

concepts.title: Sealed Types and Pattern Matching
concepts.unit: Part I — The shapes you declare
concepts.brief: Model closed business domains with sealed interfaces/classes; switch expressions and exhaustive handling; deconstruct records with record patterns.

concepts.title: Virtual Threads
concepts.unit: Part II — How you spend a thread
concepts.brief: Build simple blocking-I/O services that scale; virtual threads versus platform-thread pools; practical pitfalls: pinning, ThreadLocal, and connection-pool limits.

concepts.title: Structured Concurrency and Scoped Values
concepts.unit: Part II — How you spend a thread
concepts.brief: Coordinate concurrent work as one request-scoped unit; cancellation, deadlines, failure handling; carry request, tenant, and trace context safely. Structured concurrency is labelled preview throughout; scoped values are final on Java 25.

concepts.title: Foreign Function & Memory API
concepts.unit: Part III — What you can reach, what you can see
concepts.brief: Call a native library without classic JNI boilerplate; use memory segments and arenas safely; one small C interop example.

concepts.title: Production Performance and Observability
concepts.unit: Part III — What you can reach, what you can see
concepts.brief: Java Flight Recorder for CPU, allocations, locks, and virtual-thread activity; startup/warmup basics, AOT caches, and compact object headers; measure before tuning, and use JMH for focused benchmarks.

concepts.title: Capstone: Modernize a Small Service
concepts.brief: Start with a Java 17-style API aggregator; records for API models; sealed result types and pattern matching for outcomes; virtual threads for parallel downstream requests; structured cancellation and scoped request context; diagnose it with JFR.
